diagnosis: Repeated no-op behavior is overrepresented in candidate/bad runs, especially operations labeled result:repeated.
expected_mechanism: Detecting unchanged state prevents unproductive action loops and forces recovery or termination, improving task efficiency. The cost is a small state-comparison overhead and occasional premature strategy changes when progress is not immediately observable.
policy_text: After any no-op or unchanged-state action, do not repeat the same action unchanged. Inspect the state, revise the action or strategy, and stop with a concise blocker report if two recovery attempts produce no observable progress.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.value, (.stack_frames[] | select(startswith("action:")))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '$2=="action:noop" {if($1>0)p+=$1;else n+=-$1} {if($1>0)ap+=$1;else an+=-$1} END{printf "noop bad=%d good=%d excess=%d raw_ratio=%.3f bad_share=%.3f%% good_share=%.3f%% share_ratio=%.3f\n",p,n,p-n,p/n,100*p/ap,100*n/an,(p/ap)/(n/an)}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: No-op operations: bad=505, good=122, candidate excess=383. They comprise 6.856% of bad operations versus 3.228% of good operations, a 2.124× normalized overrepresentation.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(any(.stack_frames[]; .=="action:noop")) | [.value, (.stack_frames[]|select(startswith("result:")))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($1>0)p[$2]+=$1;else n[$2]+=-$1} END{for(k in p) printf "%s bad=%d good=%d excess=%+d\n",k,p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k]}' | sort
quantitative_evidence.finding: For no-op operations labeled result:repeated, bad=441 and good=85, yielding +356 candidate excess and a 5.19× raw ratio.
